statement: Judgmental equality. Figure 3 depicts an excerpt of the rules for judgemental equality. The rules Beta and Eta correspond to β and η equivalence. In this figure, we have elided the rules that specify that judgemental equality is an equivalence relation. The rules Delta, Zeta and Iota, respectively corresponding to unfolding definitions, expansion of let-ins and simplification of eliminators are also elided in Figure 3. The rule Iota basically states that when the term being eliminated is a constructor c applied to certain values, then the result of elimination is judgementally equal to the corresponding case-eliminator fc applied to the arguments of the constructor where (mutually) recursive arguments are appropriately eliminated. See Timany and Sozeau [19] for details. Note that the equivalence of the judgmental equality presentation and the implementation of definitional equality by conversion (as implemented in Coq) is a tricky issue and it is still an open problem to formally show equivalence for a system with cumulativity [14], we leave this to future work.
